CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py. CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The summon now passes its `slot_name=` to `CreatureCmd.add`, which re-sorts `combat.enemies` by `Encounter.slots.index(...)` exactly as `CombatManager.AddCreature` -> `CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName` does. Re-executed witness in audit/tools/, plus regression tests in test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: FogmogNormal.Slots => ["illusion", "fogmog"] (FogmogNormal.cs:15, backed by the public consts illusionSlot/fogmogSlot at :9-11). FOGMOG_NORMAL = Encounter(id='fogmog_normal', monster_classes=[Fogmog]) declares no `slots=` and no `monster_slots=` at all (both default to the empty tuple, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py). This is the mechanism's structural root: with encounter.slots empty, CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name (combat.py:1317-1337) is a documented no-op regardless of what slot_name any creature carries (combat.py:1329's `if encounter is None or not getattr(encounter, 'slots', ()): return`), so even fixing the summon call below cannot restore the game's ordering without also declaring this row. Filed as one mechanism together with GenerateMonsters below (same root cause, same fix); see GenerateMonsters for the executed witness. Mechanism id: encounter/fogmog/g1.

HasScene.rationale: Selects a bespoke Godot scene layout for this encounter (public bool => true) instead of the act's generic combat scene. Its only reader is NCombatRoom.cs:289, Godot scene instantiation -- zero gameplay effect. The headless sim renders no scene.

C#'s AllPossibleMonsters getter (FogmogNormal.cs:19-23) lists [Fogmog, EyeWithTeeth] purely for ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: The INITIAL roster half is a roster/order/draw-count match but not a slot match: FogmogNormal.GenerateMonsters (FogmogNormal.cs:25-28) returns `(ModelDb.Monster<Fogmog>().ToMutable(), "fogmog")` -- one monster, zero base.Rng calls, tagged slot 'fogmog'. FOGMOG_NORMAL.monster_classes=[Fogmog] with monster_slots=() (default) means the sim's Fogmog is never tagged with a slot name at all -- inert on its own (a single enemy has nothing to sort against), but it means the row is not seeded the way the game seeds it. The OBSERVABLE divergence is in the mid-combat summon: Fogmog.cs:60-67's IllusionMove calls `CreatureCmd.Add<EyeWithTeeth>(base.CombatState, "illusion")`, which fires CombatManager.AddCreature's SortEnemiesBySlotName (gated on a non-null SlotName) -- Slots.IndexOf("illusion")=0 < Slots.IndexOf("fogmog")=1, so the summon is re-sorted AHEAD of the starting Fogmog, giving enemy order [EyeWithTeeth, Fogmog]. The sim's fogmog.py:93-95 `_illusion_move` calls `CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, EyeWithTeeth(ctx.hooks, self._rng))` with NO slot_name, so the summon is simply appended (cmds.py:800-848's `add`, slot_name=None -> no re-sort branch taken even if the Slots gap above were fixed) -- enemy order stays [Fogmog, EyeWithTeeth], the reverse of the game's. Fogmog's move machine starts at ILLUSION_MOVE (build_machine's initial state, fogmog.py:70-91), so this fires on turn 1 of every Fogmog fight and the reordering persists for the rest of combat. Impact: Enemies[i] indices (targeting, observation encoding, camera slot) disagree with the game from turn 1 onward whenever this encounter is fought -- the same bug class the brief names for ovicopter (per-slot HP/Niche and slot-list order), found here for the first time in this encounter and NOT previously in the queue (grep of GAP-QUEUE.md found no existing fogmog or slot-order-on-summon entry). Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e1.py fogmog-slot-order` constructs the real CombatState, fires `_illusion_move` directly, and prints `[('Fogmog', 1, None), ('EyeWithTeeth', 2, None)]` -- confirming no re-sort occurs and both creatures carry slot_name=None. Mechanism id: encounter/fogmog/g1 (same as Slots above -- one fix, both hooks).

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by FogmogNormal. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

FOGMOG_NORMAL carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream)
guards.rationale: FogmogNormal.GenerateMonsters makes zero base.Rng calls (FogmogNormal.cs:25-28, confirmed by reading the whole method) and the sim's create_monsters counterpart (the default Encounter.create_monsters this unit inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) makes zero calls to any Rng/random.Random for composition -- there is nothing here for stream identity to diverge on. (Draw-count fact only; which named stream backs EncounterModel.Rng in general is seam/rng_streams' mechanism, already verdicted faithful for the seeding formula at rng_streams step 21.)
